alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers

assumptions: Crash, conflict, barrier, sidewalk, crossing, and demand data have explicit observation processes.
Accessibility is evaluated across route continuity, slope, surface, crossing, and obstruction dimensions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers.

constraints.description: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: vision-zero director and accessibility compliance officer
design.decision_question: Where do verified barriers, crossings, conflicts, speeds, and destinations break continuous safe access?

independence_key.decision_object: continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

independence_key.primary_outcome: essential destinations without a continuous safe accessible route

design.intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: essential destinations without a continuous safe accessible route
distributional gap in essential destinations without a continuous safe accessible route
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not equate request keywords or mapped sidewalks with verified accessible routes.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.
design.reference_implementation_note: Tier-D template deep.mobility.accessibility-request.v1 (Accessibility-related request planning) supplies a bounded reference workflow for this design axis. The mapping does not establish complete city-specific inputs, external validity, deployment, adoption, or impact.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for continuous pedestrian safety and accessibility barriers passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

design.title: Diagnose pedestrian safety and accessible-route breaks
transportability_risks: Street design, enforcement, mobility-device needs, exposure, and reporting vary by place.
Crash-only models underrepresent near misses and unreported accessibility barriers.

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
